text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Work-up of transient loss of consciousness: witness account, orthostatic vital signs, 12-lead ECG today, a 14-day ambulatory ECG patch from tomorrow, blood count, electrolytes, calcium, glucose, kidney and liver tests, HbA1c, lipids, and TSH; EEG and MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted and epilepsy-protocol sequences; CT angiography of the head and neck; transthoracic echocardiogram
  • Neurology consultation: is this epilepsy, syncope, or transient ischemic attack; review of the EEG, MRI, and vascular imaging; whether to start an antiseizure medicine and which; stroke prevention; and driving
  • Seizure safety from today: no driving until a seizure-free period set by state law and his neurologist; showers rather than baths; no swimming or riding alone; no climbing to heights; regular sleep of at least seven hours; a written seizure action plan for his staff, including when to call emergency services
  • Blood pressure: lisinopril 10 mg daily from today; home blood pressure log twice daily; potassium and creatinine in two weeks; target below 130/80 mmHg
  • Antiseizure medicine: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, with teaching about irritability, low mood, and drowsiness; a seizure diary; no missed doses
  • Secondary stroke prevention for the cortical infarct: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg at bedtime with a lipid panel at 4 to 12 weeks (LDL target below 70 mg/dL), blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg with a second drug if needed, a home sleep apnea test, and a further four weeks of ambulatory rhythm monitoring (more than 30 days in all) for occult atrial fibrillation
  • Lifestyle: Mediterranean-style diet with sodium below 2.3 g a day; aerobic activity at least 150 minutes a week; alcohol kept at his present low level; no tobacco
  • Mood and cognition after the diagnosis: PHQ-9 four weeks after starting levetiracetam and then periodically; MoCA in the first months after the infarct was found
  • Adult prevention plan: influenza, pneumococcal, and recombinant zoster vaccines; hepatitis C, hepatitis B, and HIV screening; colonoscopy for colorectal cancer screening; eye examination; PSA discussion at 55

resource.title: Julius Caesar synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluation of recurrent transient episodes of collapse in a 54-year-old man, separating seizure from convulsive syncope and transient ischemic attack (history from a witness, orthostatic vital signs, ECG and ambulatory cardiac monitoring under the ACC/AHA/HRS 2017 syncope guideline; EEG and MRI with diffusion-weighted and epilepsy-protocol sequences; CT angiography of the head and neck and echocardiography), and the diagnosis of late-onset focal epilepsy with a structural vascular cause from a clinically unrecognized cortical infarct, classified by the ILAE 2017 seizure and epilepsy classifications and the ILAE 2014 practical definition. Management follows the AAN/AES 2015 first-seizure guideline (recurrence risk and the case for treatment), the AAN/AES 2018 guideline on newer antiseizure medicines (levetiracetam, with mood monitoring), and the AHA/ASA 2021 secondary stroke prevention guideline with the CMID stroke, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia monographs (aspirin, high-intensity atorvastatin to an LDL below 70 mg/dL, blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg, 30-day rhythm monitoring, depression and cognitive screening), together with seizure safety and driving restrictions, an intercurrent respiratory infection, and an adult preventive visit. The historical dispute between epilepsy and cerebrovascular disease stays unresolved (R); the modern episode makes no claim about what he had.
